Recording a deed with the Madison County Judge of Probate

Deeds and mortgages in Madison County are recorded at the Judge of Probate's office, and a buyer has no public notice of ownership until the deed is filed there. The office sits in the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, Huntsville, in the same building as the tax collector and the Board of Equalization.

Alabama counties pack several jobs into one office. The probate judge handles estates too, and in Madison County the probate staff also records the documents that move title. Staff cannot give legal advice, so questions about wording a deed go to an attorney or closing agent.

For a seller, recording is the last step. The title company prepares the deed, collects the recording charges and the deed tax at closing, and files the paperwork.

Recording fees

The posted schedule adds up to $25.75 for the first page of a document and $2.50 for each page after that. Call the office to confirm the current charges before you count on an exact figure.

ChargeAmount
Imaging fee$10.00
Per page$2.50
Filing fee$1.00
Microfilm$0.25
Mental health fee$12.00
Total, first page$25.75
Each additional page$2.50

If a separate sales validation form is attached, it is one more page at $2.50. All of this comes before the deed tax.

Alabama deed tax in Madison County

The deed tax is $0.50 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, which is $1.00 per $1,000. Madison County prints it as 50 cents per $500, figured on the appraised value or the purchase price, with a minimum of 50 cents when the purchase is 100% financed.

The rule is section 40-22-1 of the Code of Alabama. It taxes only the value above any mortgage or vendor's lien that has already paid mortgage tax. Of what the probate judge collects, two thirds goes to the state treasury and one third to the county treasury. Your closing agent will run the actual number for your sale.

Some instruments are exempt: transfers of mortgages that already paid mortgage tax, deeds for nominal consideration meant to perfect title, and re-recorded corrected instruments.

The RT-1 sales validation form

Deeds recorded in Madison County must come with the RT-1 Real Estate Sales Validation form unless the same information is written into the deed. It has been required since August 1, 2012, and the county charges an extra $2.50 page fee when the form is recorded. Correction deeds are exempt.

Section 40-22-1 is behind the rule: it calls for proof of the actual purchase price, or the actual value if the property was not sold. The Department of Revenue developed the form, and a person who signs it in good faith does not have to supply more documentation. Someone who intentionally refuses to give proof after a specific request, or gives false proof, owes a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax due, whichever is greater.

If no proof is offered at all, the probate judge computes the tax from the latest assessment, and the penalty can apply. The easy way to stay clear of trouble is to make the settlement statement and the RT-1 show the same price.

What a document needs to be recorded

A deed that misses one of the county's requirements can be turned away at the counter.

  • Originals are required, and copies from other courts must be certified.
  • Every document carries the name and address of whoever prepared it.
  • Grantor marital status appears on all deeds, and mortgagor status on mortgages.
  • Checks are payable to Judge of Probate, Madison County, Alabama.
  • Mailed documents need an adequately sized self-addressed stamped envelope and a 3-inch margin at the top of the first page.

Electronic recording runs through two approved vendors, Simplifile and CSC, and e-recording stops at 4 p.m. daily. Clerks cannot fill in blanks on a document. When two documents must record in order, such as a deed and then a second mortgage, wait for the first to come back before uploading the next. Call ahead for a transaction that spans several counties.

Name indexing and extra charges

Madison County indexes two grantors, two grantees and two cross-references free. Each additional name or reference costs $1, and the county counts more than people toward that limit: a/k/a and d/b/a names, trusts and trustees, administrators and personal representatives, the estate of a deceased person, MERS, and companies listed as manager, member or partner. An inherited house sold by an estate, or an LLC property with several managers, can pick up a few of these small charges.

Other items on the posted schedule:

  • Certified copies cost $1 per page plus $2 for certification.
  • Mortgage tax is 15 cents per $100, or $1.50 per $1,000, rounded up to the next $100.
  • Mortgages and deeds to exempt entities carry an additional 50 cent no tax stamp fee.
  • Releases, assignments, affidavits, liens and powers of attorney use the same basic recording fees as deeds.

When a deed and mortgage are filed together

If a deed and a mortgage record at the same time, deed tax is owed on the down payment or equity, not the full price. When the whole price is financed, the deed tax falls to the 50 cent minimum.

A deed filed with a tax-exempt mortgage is the exception: the deed tax is figured on the full purchase price or appraised value. Confirm the deed and mortgage consideration in the e-recording system before you submit.

A cash sale is simpler. With no lender there is no mortgage tax, and the transaction usually needs only the deed, the validation form and the recording charges.

Madison County housing context

Madison County is the second most populous county in Alabama, with 388,153 residents counted in 2020, and Huntsville is the county seat. The 2020 census shows 169,820 housing units, about 7.1% of them vacant, and 33.7% of occupied homes are rented.

Not every deed here is routine. Houses inherited through an estate, homes with tenants, and properties with unpaid taxes need extra steps, and the probate office is where those steps end.

Papers for a probate-related sale

The probate judge's office handles estates as well as land records, so an heir selling an inherited house may deal with both desks. Ask the office or an attorney which estate papers apply to your situation. Bring or gather these:

  • The prior deed or title information showing how the owner held the property.
  • Any estate paperwork the office or your attorney says applies, when the owner has died.
  • The deed itself, with preparer details and grantor marital status.
  • The RT-1 or matching price language in the deed.
  • Payment for the recording fee and deed tax.

We buy houses in Madison County as they are, including inherited and tax-delinquent homes.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I record a deed in Madison County, AL?

At the Judge of Probate in the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, Huntsville, or electronically through an approved vendor such as Simplifile or CSC.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Madison County?

The posted schedule is $25.75 for the first page and $2.50 for each additional page, plus deed tax. Call the office to confirm current charges.

What is the Alabama deed tax?

$0.50 per $500 of value or fraction, which is $1.00 per $1,000, under Code of Alabama section 40-22-1. The minimum is $0.50.

Do I need an RT-1 form in Madison County?

Yes, unless the same information is written into the deed. The form carries an extra $2.50 page fee and does not apply to correction deeds.

Can the probate office help me write a deed?

No. Staff are prohibited by law from giving legal advice, so use an attorney or closing agent.

Role of the Jefferson County Judge of Probate

Jefferson County's Judge of Probate oversees the office that files deeds and mortgages into the permanent land records. After a house is sold, the deed lands here, the deed tax is paid, and the new ownership gets indexed.

This court also supervises estates. An inherited house can therefore visit the building twice: once while the estate is settled and again at resale. Staff members cannot draft or correct a deed, and they won't advise you on the law. People who need a deed written are referred to a lawyer.

Probate office locations and hours

Two divisions serve the county, one in Birmingham and one in Bessemer. A single Probate Judge, Deputy Probate Judge and Chief Clerk oversee both, and the counters are open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays.

  • Birmingham division: 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd., Birmingham, AL 35203.
  • Bessemer division: 1801 3rd Avenue North, Bessemer, AL 35020.

Bessemer sits roughly 16 miles southwest of Birmingham by road. Not sure where your paperwork belongs? Phone the Probate Court at (205) 325-5203 first.

Jefferson County at a glance

With 674,721 residents in the 2020 census and a 2025 estimate of 665,742, Jefferson is Alabama's most populous county. Municipalities include Birmingham, Bessemer, Hoover, Homewood, Vestavia Hills, Mountain Brook, Trussville, Gardendale, Fultondale, Hueytown, Pleasant Grove and Center Point.

Some of these cities straddle a county line: Birmingham, Hoover, Helena, Vestavia Hills, Leeds and Trussville each spill into a neighboring county. Before you head to a courthouse, confirm which county holds your parcel. A deed filed in the wrong office costs you days at closing.

Deed tax and recording costs

Expect the state deed tax to come to 50 cents per $500 of value (Code of Alabama section 40-22-1). When the deal includes a mortgage that already paid mortgage tax, the taxable amount can shrink. Per-page recording charges are added separately and differ by document type.

The statute adds a few rules for closing week:

  • A deed must be accompanied by proof of the real purchase price on the Department of Revenue form.
  • Withholding that proof after a request triggers a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater.
  • Two thirds of what is collected goes to the state treasury, one third to the county.
  • A deed for nominal consideration, given only to perfect title, owes no tax. Clerks stamp it "No Tax Collected."

Look for the exact charge on your settlement statement. The sales contract decides who pays it.

What clerks can and can't do for you

What clerks can do is point you to the public index. Whether a lien is attached to your property is a question they leave to a title company or attorney.

The records can be searched online or in person. LANDMARK WEB subscribers can look up land records and view images of select documents, and the clerks give free training on site. Plenty of documents can be opened on the website without charge, and uncertified printouts cost a small fee.

ServiceCost
Copies made in the Record Room$1.00 per page
Plat copies$15.00 per page
Certification of a copy$2.00 more per document

Bring a card, cash, a cashier's check, a money order or a business check. A local personal check works with ID.

Paperwork to gather before listing

  • The deed, or the estate papers that show how title reached you.
  • Payoff letters from each lender with a mortgage on the house.
  • Photo ID for every person who will sign.
  • The sales contract, since the price sets both the deed tax and the required value statement.
  • Divorce decrees or court orders touching title. Decrees get recorded and indexed with land records, but not every court filing ends up there.

If a relative who owned the house has died, settle the estate first. Whoever handles closing will ask who is authorized to sign for the owner.

After closing: assessment and property tax

New owners deal with the county in three stages. File the deed with probate, get the parcel assessed in your name at the revenue office, and apply for any exemption you qualify for.

Alabama property tax is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after December 31. Bills follow whoever owned the parcel the previous October 1, so a bill arriving after the sale may still show the seller. Hand any such bill to the title company or the buyer.

Typical path of a sale through the probate office

Whoever handles the closing normally prepares the deed and combs the record for liens. You sign, and the paperwork is carried to the probate office with the value statement, tax and fee. Once recorded, the buyer appears as owner in the land records.

The clerks can't repair a deed, so a misspelled name or wrong legal description goes back to the lawyer who prepared it. Request a copy of the recorded deed and file it with your closing documents.

When the seller has died, the estate must prove who holds signing authority, and that proof normally comes from this same probate court. Begin early. A buyer with a set closing date will not wait for letters that haven't been issued.

If the title search turns up an old lien or an unsigned release, closing stalls until it is cleared. Ask what was found and who must act, then keep a dated list of open items and check in weekly.

Inherited houses and the probate court

Heirs often meet the Probate Court twice with the same house. The first visit is about the estate: who is in charge of it and who owns what. The second comes when the property changes hands and the deed is filed. Different clerks may help with each, but the building and the judge are the same.

Out-of-state heirs can save trips by calling (205) 325-5203 and asking which division handles their file. Put questions in writing where you can, and log who you spoke to and on what day. The buyer's title company will want those estate papers before it agrees to close.

Common Jefferson County seller situations

Neighborhoods differ widely here, and so do the headaches.

  • Older homes in former mill and mining communities such as Ensley, North Birmingham and Woodlawn, once separate towns and now Birmingham neighborhoods.
  • Inherited houses with heirs living out of state.
  • Parcels close to a county line, where the right probate office is unclear.
  • Vacant houses with unpaid tax or code problems.
  • Owners in a hurry who can't wait on a retail buyer's loan approval.

Cash Home Buyers puts written offers on Jefferson County houses in their current condition. A local title company handles the recording. A cash sale avoids appraisal and lender repair demands, yet the deed still passes through this office.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I record a deed in Jefferson County, Alabama?

At the Probate Court of Jefferson County, either the Birmingham division (716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd.) or the Bessemer division (1801 3rd Avenue North). Both are open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays.

How much is the Alabama deed tax?

It is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 (Code of Alabama section 40-22-1). The amount can be reduced where mortgage tax was already paid on a loan that stays with the property.

Can the Jefferson County probate office prepare my deed?

No. Staff can't draft or revise a deed or advise you on the law, so you will need an attorney.

Can the recording office tell me if there is a lien on my house?

No. Clerks can't run a title search. A title company or attorney handles that.

How much does a copy of a recorded deed cost?

Record Room copies are $1.00 per page and plat copies are $15.00 per page. Certifying a copy adds $2.00 per document.

What does the Shelby County judge of probate do when a house is sold?

The judge of probate is the county officer who takes a signed deed into the public record and collects the state's recordation tax on it. Alabama's section 40-22-1 says a deed or similar instrument cannot be received for record until the privilege tax is paid.

The Department of Revenue tells new owners to record the deed in the probate office and then assess the property at the county revenue office, bringing the deed along. For a Shelby County sale, that means two stops after closing: probate for the record, then the property tax office for the assessment.

Call the office or read its current fee sheet before you plan a closing date.

How is the deed tax figured on a Shelby County deed?

The tax is 50 cents for every $500 of value conveyed, or fraction of $500, and it is figured on the actual price paid. Under section 40-22-1(c), only the value above a mortgage or vendor's lien that has already paid mortgage tax is taxable.

The deed must arrive with proof of the real price, on a form the Department of Revenue develops, and the person signing attests that it is accurate in good faith. If no proof is given, the judge of probate bases the tax on the latest assessed value and adds a penalty. The statute sets that penalty at $100 or 25 percent of the tax actually due, whichever is greater, for someone who intentionally withholds proof after being asked.

ItemWhat section 40-22-1 says
Rate$0.50 per $500 of value or fraction
Tax baseActual price, less mortgage or lien that paid mortgage tax
Split of the taxTwo thirds to the state, one third to the county
Penalty for withheld proof$100 or 25 percent of tax due, whichever is greater
No tax requiredNominal-consideration title-perfecting deeds, corrected deeds, mortgage transfers that already paid

Which deeds are exempt, and what happens to a deed that spans two counties?

Several instruments carry no recordation tax. The statute lists deeds written for nominal consideration to perfect title, the re-recording of corrected instruments, and transfers of mortgages on which the mortgage tax was paid. When a deed is exempt, the judge of probate stamps it "No Tax Collected."

A deed covering land in two or more counties follows a separate route. The probate judge certifies the instrument to the Department of Revenue, which sets the value in each county. The filer can deposit an estimated amount to get the deed recorded right away, and any excess is refunded once the value is fixed.

That rule matters in Shelby County because several places straddle county lines. Vestavia Hills, Hoover, Helena, Leeds and Calera are each partly in another county, per the county's Wikipedia entry. A title company will check whether your parcel sits entirely inside one county.

Where is Shelby County and how big is it?

Shelby County sits in central Alabama, and its county seat is Columbiana. Wikipedia's county entry gives a total area of 810 square miles, 785 of them land, and names Alabaster as the largest city.

The county was established on February 7, 1818, and named for Isaac Shelby. The first seat was Shelbyville, in what is now Pelham. The seat moved to Columbia, now Columbiana, in 1826, and the current limestone courthouse was built from 1905 to 1906. The 1854 brick courthouse is now the Shelby County Museum and Archives.

Shelby County borders six other counties:

  • St. Clair County to the northeast
  • Talladega County to the east
  • Coosa County to the southeast
  • Chilton County to the south
  • Bibb County to the southwest
  • Jefferson County to the northwest

How fast has Shelby County grown?

Shelby County's population grew from 66,298 in 1980 to 223,024 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 238,552. For the 2020 census the county had 84,241 households and 89,060 housing units, and 78.1 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied.

Growth followed the roads. Interstate 65 and U.S. 31 link the county to Jefferson County, and Wikipedia ties suburban growth in Pelham, Helena, Alabaster and Chelsea to that access. Other major routes are U.S. 231, U.S. 280 and several state roads.

The county's economy was farm-based for a long time. Soybeans have passed cotton as the main crop since about 1990, and that the county once hosted an early inland waterway on the Coosa River and an early east-west railroad. The county page lists CSX, Norfolk Southern and the Calera and Shelby Railroad among its railroads.

For a seller, the practical advice is to bring a signed deed, a correct legal description and a completed value form, because a deed that needs corrections costs time at the counter.

What land and schools define Shelby County?

The county is partly hilly and partly flat. Oak Mountain and Double Oak Mountain are the southern tail of the Appalachians, while much of the rest is farmland and pasture with lowlands along two rivers. The Cahaba River runs along the northern edge and the Coosa River valley takes in the east. Lay Lake is a large reservoir that borders Shelby and three other counties.

Schools are split among several systems. Shelby County Schools serves areas outside Hoover, Alabaster and Pelham, while Alabaster City Schools, Pelham City Schools and Hoover City Schools serve their own cities. Higher education includes the University of Montevallo and a Jefferson State Community College campus.

If you own property near a lake, river or the Cahaba, ask your insurer and the county about flood maps before you list.

What do Shelby County sellers run into at the probate office?

The common snags are about the paper, not the house. Watch for these:

  • A deed that names the wrong legal description or a misspelled owner, which may need a corrected deed.
  • No proof of the purchase price, which triggers the value penalty.
  • An unpaid property tax bill, since Alabama taxes turn delinquent after December 31.
  • An owner who has died, where the estate may need a court order before the house can be conveyed.

Alabama counties are not required to mail tax notices, so an owner who never received a bill is still responsible. A buyer should check payment status with the county before the deed is recorded.

Cash buyers pay the same tax and the same recording costs as anyone else. What a cash sale changes is the repair list and the wait for a buyer's lender, not the recording steps.

Frequently asked questions

Who records deeds in Shelby County, Alabama?

The judge of probate. The Alabama Department of Revenue tells buyers to record the deed in the probate office and then assess the property at the county revenue office.

What is the Alabama deed tax rate?

Fifty cents for each $500 of value conveyed, or fraction of $500, under section 40-22-1, less any mortgage or lien that already paid mortgage tax. Two thirds goes to the state and one third to the county.

Do I need to show the sale price when I record a Shelby County deed?

Yes. The deed must come with proof of the actual purchase price, using a Department of Revenue form. Intentionally withholding it after a request carries a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater.

Is any deed recorded without tax?

Some are. Deeds for nominal consideration that perfect title, corrected deeds and mortgage transfers that already paid tax are listed as exceptions, and the probate judge stamps them "No Tax Collected."

What are the recording fees in Shelby County?

Ask the Shelby County probate office for the current schedule before closing.
